## The Science of Salary Negotiation

A study of 10,000 job offer negotiations found that candidates who negotiate receive 13% higher compensation on average. Yet 55% of candidates accept the first offer without discussion.

### Tactics That Work (Data-Backed)

| Tactic | Avg Increase | Success Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Anchoring with specific number | +14% | 72% |
| Citing market data | +11% | 68% |
| Presenting competing offers | +18% | 65% |
| Negotiating beyond base salary | +9% (total comp) | 78% |
| Asking for time to consider | +7% | 82% |
| Expressing enthusiasm first | +5% | 85% |

### Tactics That Backfire

| Tactic | Avg Impact | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Ultimatums | -4% or offer rescinded | 23% offer withdrawal |
| Lying about competing offers | 0% or relationship damage | High |
| Excessive back-and-forth (3+ rounds) | -2% | Negotiation fatigue |
| Negotiating before receiving offer | -8% | Perceived as presumptuous |

### The Negotiation Script

Step 1 : Express genuine enthusiasm for the role

Looking for your next opportunity?

Create a free profile and get matched with companies hiring in your field. No fees, no spam.

[Create your profile](/candidate/auth)
[Browse open roles](/jobs)

"I'm really excited about this opportunity. The team, the mission, and the growth trajectory all align with what I'm looking for."

Step 2 : Present your research

"Based on my research of market rates for this role in this geography, and considering my [specific experience], I was hoping we could discuss the compensation."

Step 3 : Name your number

"I was targeting a base salary of $X, based on [market data source]."

Step 4 : Listen and collaborate

"I understand there may be constraints. I'm open to discussing the total package — signing bonus, equity, professional development budget, and flexibility are all valuable to me."

### Beyond Base Salary

Negotiable components many candidates forget:

- Signing bonus (one-time, often easier for companies to approve)
- Equity / RSUs
- Professional development budget
- Remote work days
- Review timeline (6 months vs. 12 months for first raise)
- PTO days
- Title (which affects future earning potential)

### Use Market Data

Check salary benchmarks in our salary explorer tools and industry-specific compensation data . Knowledge is your strongest negotiation asset.
